1.explanation: The bug is specifically about how Markdown tables are printed and how their separator lines are generated in the presence of long content. The function printTable in src/language-markdown/printer-markdown.js is almost certainly responsible for rendering Markdown tables, including deciding the length and style of separator lines. To fix the bug, logic needs to be introduced into this function to detect when a table row would be excessively long and to fall back to a simpler separator line style (such as always using three-dash patterns like | :---: |), rather than extending the dashes to match the longest cell content. None of the other compressed files (options.js, parser-markdown.js) relate to printing tables, so only printTable is relevant here.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario involves Prettier formatting Markdown tables in a way that produces extremely long lines, especially when table cells contain lots of HTML or long content. This can result in table separator lines (like the --- lines) that are as long as the longest cell content, which is visually unwieldy and makes editing or reviewing such files difficult. The attached image shows such a file, with a table separator line that is 865 characters long, matching the length of a very long table cell.

The function printTable in src/language-markdown/printer-markdown.js is almost certainly responsible for generating the markdown table output, including the separator lines. To fix the bug, logic must be added or adjusted in printTable to detect when a table row or separator would exceed a certain length and, in those cases, use the standard three-dash separator pattern instead of one that matches the cell content length. 2.bug_scenario: The bug scenario, as shown in the image and described in the report, is that when Prettier formats markdown tables with very long content in cells (such as those containing HTML or all-contributors tables), the length of the separator line (the line of dashes and colons between the header and body of the table) becomes extremely long—matching the length of the longest cell content. This leads to unreasonably long lines (865 characters in the example), which is undesirable for readability and version control. The expected behavior is that Prettier should detect such cases and use a fallback separator (like '| :---: | :---: | ... |') to avoid excessive line length.
